I reviewed `artifacts\editorial\release-candidates\transit\translink-july-fare-increase-what-riders-pay.mdx` (the only file matching that slug) against the research capture, learning log, scorecard, image asset, and the prior published-transit review. Note: my tools (Read/Grep/Glob) cannot compute a hash, so I could not independently recompute the SHA-256; findings refer to the file at that path as it exists now.

**Factual support and source use.** Every fare number matches the recorded source capture in `artifacts\editorial\research\2026-07-19-evening-transit-burnaby-candidates.json` (captured 2026-07-19T16:58 via live HTML extraction) exactly: the 5% average July 1 increase; adult cash/contactless $3.50/$5.10/$6.70 with +$0.15/+$0.25/+$0.10; adult Stored Value $2.85/$4.20/$5.40 with +$0.15/+$0.20/+$0.30; concession $2.30/$3.40/$4.60; monthly passes $117.20/$156.70/$211.65 and $66.95 concession; DayPasses $12.55/$9.75; the $6.50 YVR AddFare at YVR-Airport, Sea Island Centre, and Templeton; 90-minute validity; and buses/HandyDART as 1-Zone at all times. All claims are attributed to TransLink's pricing page, which is the sole listed source and appropriate for a fare bulletin.

**Title/meta/structure/usefulness.** Title, subtitle, and description accurately describe the content and don't overreach; the description covers exactly what the body delivers (cash, Compass, passes, DayPass, AddFare). Slug matches the filename, category `transit` matches the directory, readingTime 2 fits ~330 words. Structure is a clean utility bulletin: headline numbers first, then planning caveats (zone timing, airport AddFare, bus-cash transfer warning), which serves the stated readerImpact.

**Image/frontmatter integrity.** `public\images\editorial\2026\07\translink-july-fare-increase-2026.png` exists, depicts a rider tapping a contactless card at a fare-gate reader with blue Metro Vancouver-style buses behind — matching the alt text — and uses a generic card logo rather than actual Compass/TransLink marks. Attribution correctly discloses it as an original generated editorial image. Frontmatter fields match the sibling transit release candidate's schema.

**Legal/reputational risk.** Low. Public fare data, consistently attributed ("TransLink's page says…"), no individuals or trademarks reproduced.

Minor, non-blocking observations: (1) A few secondary claims are not in the recorded capture facts — the 6:30 p.m./weekend/holiday 1-Zone rule, DayPass invalidity on West Coast Express, concession eligibility (HandyCard, seniors 65+, youth 13–18), the bus-cash non-transferability warning, and the "unless an exemption applies" hedge. All are long-standing, stable TransLink fare policies consistent with the source page and are attributed rather than asserted independently. (2) The frontmatter `publishedAt` (16:40 PT) predates the recorded capture time (16:58 PT); worth refreshing the timestamp at promotion. (3) The +$0.10 cash 3-Zone increase is well under the stated 5% average — it matches the capture verbatim and is attributed to TransLink, so it reads as the agency's own rounding, not an article error. None of these warrant holding publication.
